back: The study of valid reasoning and argumentation
A statement that is either true or false
An argument where if the premises are true the conclusion must be true
A valid argument with actually true premises
Reasoning from general premises to a specific conclusion with certainty
Reasoning from specific observations to general conclusions with probability
A logical argument with two premises and a conclusion
If P then Q; P is true; therefore Q is true
If P then Q; Q is false; therefore P is false

front: What is the law of non-contradiction?
back: Something cannot be both true and false at the same time

front: What is the law of excluded middle?
back: A proposition must be either true or false with no third option
An error in reasoning that undermines the logic of an argument
Attacking the person making the argument rather than the argument itself

front: What is a straw man fallacy?
back: Misrepresenting someone's argument to make it easier to attack
Presenting only two options when more exist
Using the conclusion as a premise in the argument

front: What is an appeal to authority?
back: Arguing something is true because an authority figure says so

front: What is the slippery slope fallacy?
back: Claiming one event will inevitably lead to extreme consequences without justification

front: What is a conjunction in logic?
back: A compound statement using AND (true only if both parts are true)

front: What is a disjunction in logic?
back: A compound statement using OR (true if at least one part is true)
The logical operation that reverses the truth value of a proposition
An if-then statement (if P then Q)

front: What is the converse of "if P then Q"?
back: If Q then P (not logically equivalent to the original)

front: What is the contrapositive of "if P then Q"?
back: If not Q then not P (logically equivalent to the original)
A statement that is true under all possible interpretations
A statement that is false under all possible interpretations
Logic that analyzes the internal structure of propositions using quantifiers and predicates
Symbol ∀ meaning "for all" or "for every"
Symbol ∃ meaning "there exists" or "for some"
A condition that must be true for something else to be true (Q is necessary for P: if P then Q)
